episodes.214059: Strong thunderstorms moved through Petroleum and southern Phillips Counties, a few of which became severe.
episodes.214232: On the afternoon of the 12th, numerous thunderstorm outflow boundaries collided across the South Plains of West Texas. A very unstable atmosphere allowed scattered thunderstorms to develop. Although most of these storms were non-severe, a few severe wind gusts did occur across Lubbock County. A wet microburst occurred south of Idalou (Lubbock County) which caused roof damage to a barn and mobile homes. One outflow boundary over Lubbock County was slow moving which generated slow moving thunderstorms. Localized areas of heavy rainfall occurred over northwestern portions of the city of Lubbock and the city of Slaton where multiple vehicles became stalled in flood waters.
episodes.214288: The frontal boundary from 7/12 remained stalled near the southeastern Midlands of SC into the CSRA through the day on 7/13. The environment in proximity to this front was conducive for flash flooding as slow moving convection exhibited efficient rain rates up to 2-4/hr. This brought flash flooding across Evans and Martinez GA during the evening  with additional locations of flash flooding in the Midlands of SC.
episodes.214289: The frontal boundary from 7/12 remained stalled near the southeastern Midlands of SC into the CSRA through the day on 7/13. The environment in proximity to this front was conducive for flash flooding as slow moving convection exhibited efficient rain rates up to 2-4/hr. This brought flash flooding across Evans and Martinez GA during the evening  with additional locations of flash flooding in the Midlands of SC.
episodes.214302: Monsoon storms formed on the afternoon of July 12th producing damaging winds and heavy rain that led to flash flooding.
episodes.214710: July 12th marked the beginning of multiple days of heavy rainfall that led to flash flooding across west Texas and southeast New Mexico. A slow-moving trough made its way towards the region from the east throughout the week, undercutting and displacing an upper-level ridge. This trough interacted with ample moisture across the area, producing showers and thunderstorms that produced heavy rainfall. On the 12th, flash flooding was mainly reported in Scurry County near Snyder.
episodes.214711: A slow-moving trough continued to make its way towards the region on July 13th. This trough once again interacted with ample moisture across the area, producing showers and thunderstorms that led to flash flooding across mainly the Lower Trans-Pecos and in portions of the Permian Basin.
episodes.214756: A broad area of high pressure shifted sufficiently to allow moisture to creep into Utah, and in combination with strong daytime heating, resulted in daily convection with instances of severe and damaging wind gusts, as well as some flooding.
episodes.214774: The synoptic pattern shifted by mid July sufficiently to allow a more marked influx of monsoonal moisture into Utah. In addition to some isolated thunderstorm wind gusts, this resulted in numerous instances of flash flooding and debris flows.
episodes.214951: Multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms produced several wind gusts in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.215271: Despite drier air aloft affecting portions of the area thanks to the Saharan Air Layer, enough moisture and instability was in place for scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms to develop across northeast FL. Southwest flow mainly focus isolated strong to severe convection over the eastern half of the region. Presence of dry air aloft likely played into stronger downbursts and areas of wind damage across northeast FL.
episodes.215565: A large cluster of stationary thunderstorms produced heavy rainfall across portions of southeast Georgia. The most intense rainfall impacted the Hinesville area and a couple of nearby public weather stations reports around 5 inches of rain over a 3 hour period. This intense rainfall produced a few instances of flash flooding in and around Hinesville.
episodes.215582: Isolated thunderstorms developed across southeast South Carolina in the late afternoon and early evening hours. One storm in northern Berkeley County became strong enough to produce a damaging wind gust in the Saint Stephen area.
episodes.216183: Behind a back door cold front, widespread showers and thunderstorms developed from the late afternoon through the early overnight hours. Numerous reports of flash flooding were reported, along with several damaging wind reports.
episodes.216184: Behind a cold front across South Carolina, showers and storms focused over the southern Piedmont and Sandhills of central North Carolina. Isolated flash flooding was reported in Stanly and Richmond Counties.
episodes.216393: A slow moving upper low approached from the northwest on the 12th, pushing a frontal boundary through the area late in the day and sparking off yet another day of widespread showers and thunderstorms across the southern Appalachian region. This resulted in some scattered reports of flash flooding in East Tennessee.
episodes.216517: Increasing moisture and instability developed isolated thunderstorms across North-Central MT during the afternoon. Strong synoptic winds and hot and dry surface conditions brought a favorable environment for gusty dry downbursts.
episodes.216588: Onshore westerly sea breeze flow and a shortwave aloft swinging across the SE U.S. combined to produce a broken line of convection that produced strong marine wind gusts near the mouth of Tampa Bay and over the Nature Coast waters near Cedar Key.
episodes.216589: Onshore westerly sea breeze flow and a shortwave aloft approaching the SE U.S. combined to produce early afternoon convection that produced a strong marine wind gust near Cedar Key.
episodes.216665: During mid-July, a slow-moving easterly wave brought sufficient moisture and lift to trigger showers and thunderstorms across portions of Central and North Texas. Flash flooding occurred in multiple areas due to the influx of tropical moisture, weak flow aloft, and slow storm movement.
episodes.216791: Multiple minor disturbances moving around an upper level ridge of high pressure over the Upper Midwest initiated thunderstorms which crossed Lake Superior from the northwest.
episodes.216792: Weak disturbances moving around an upper level ridge of high pressure brought thunderstorms to the U.P., initiating over Lake Superior and reaching the northern portion of Green Bay during the afternoon.
episodes.216795: A surge of monsoon moisture brought strong thunderstorms to the Kingman area.
episodes.216796: A surge of monsoon moisture brought strong thunderstorms to the Nevada National Security Site.
episodes.216831: A severe thunderstorm moving offshore produced wind gusts and damage.
episodes.216833: Thunderstorms produced strong to severe wind gusts at the coast.
episodes.216868: A stationary front was convectively reinforced south across East Texas to just north of the I-20 corridor, as well as North Louisiana during the morning hours of July 13th, ahead of bands of showers and thunderstorms that developed and moved east along the front from North into East Texas. The morning storms produced heavy rainfall which led to localized flooding in Smith County before diminishing, although the presence of the surface boundary and a weak upper level disturbance extending from Eastern Texas across North Louisiana into the Tennessee Valley contributed to large scale forcing within a hot, moist, and unstable air mass for the development of additional showers and thunderstorms across these areas during the mid and late afternoon. Given the weak steering currents, these storms were slow moving, and produced very heavy rainfall in a short period of time, leading to instances of flash flooding across portions of East Texas and Northwest Louisiana. Rainfall totals of 1-3 inches, with isolated totals in excess of 6 inches, were observed before the storms diminished during the evening.
episodes.216871: A stationary front was convectively reinforced south across East Texas to just north of the I-20 corridor, as well as North Louisiana during the morning hours of July 13th, ahead of bands of showers and thunderstorms that developed and moved east along the front from North into East Texas. The morning storms produced heavy rainfall which led to localized flooding in Smith County before diminishing, although the presence of the surface boundary and a weak upper level disturbance extending from Eastern Texas across North Louisiana into the Tennessee Valley contributed to large scale forcing within a hot, moist, and unstable air mass for the development of additional showers and thunderstorms across these areas during the mid and late afternoon. Given the weak steering currents, these storms were slow moving, and produced very heavy rainfall in a short period of time, leading to instances of flash flooding across portions of East Texas and Northwest Louisiana. Rainfall totals of 1-3 inches, with isolated totals in excess of 6 inches, were observed before the storms diminished during the evening.
episodes.216897: Upper level troughing remained over southwest Louisiana during multiple days in mid July. This allowed scattered storms to develop each day with some producing heavy rain.
episodes.216933: A slow-moving frontal boundary was stalled north of the Gulf Coast. At the same time,  an upper-level weakness maintained an unusually active marine convective pattern. With relatively weak background winds, the primary hazards over the coastal waters came from thunderstorms. Repeated clusters of convection produced localized strong wind gusts across the offshore waters.
episodes.217262: An upper level disturbance arrived and lingered over South Florida in early to mid June which produced a period of unsettled weather.
episodes.217292: Continuing an active monsoon period with multiple recorded wind gusts of 58 to 67 mph in Pima and Cochise counties. The severe thunderstorm winds caused damage to power equipment that caused power outages in the Tucson Metro. Additionally, the heavy rainfall caused running washes that led to 2 water rescues in the Tucson Metro and impassable roadways.
episodes.217293: Continuing an active monsoon period with multiple recorded wind gusts of 50 to 62 mph in Pima, Cochise, and Pinal counties. The severe thunderstorm winds caused damage to power equipment that caused power outages in Bisbee. Additionally, the heavy rainfall caused running washes that led to 1 water rescue in the Tucson Metro and impassable roadways.
episodes.217334: A line of storms crossed from north to south during the early morning hours on the 13th.
episodes.217335: A line of storms dropped through northern Michigan from north to south through the overnight hours, resulting in some gusty winds and hail, particularly near Onaway and Black Lake.
episodes.217396: Damaging winds associated with isolated strong to marginally severe, mostly afternoon and evening, thunderstorms were observed across portions of central Mississippi. Heavy rains from slow moving thunderstorms resulted in isolated flash flooding.
